subject: maths
printing: Part I: Reprint 2026-27; Part II: First Edition December 2025
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Square numbers and their patterns
outcomes: Learner can identify square numbers, describe patterns in them (last digits, odd-number sums) and decide if a number is a perfect square
misconceptions: Thinks squaring means doubling (5² = 10)
Believes a number ending in 6 must be a perfect square
hooks: Arrange 49 students in a square for PT drill

topics.title: Square roots
outcomes: Learner can find square roots by prime factorisation and estimation
misconceptions: Thinks √(a + b) = √a + √b
hooks: Side of a square plot with area 625 m²

topics.title: Cubes and cube roots
outcomes: Learner can identify perfect cubes, find cube roots by prime factorisation and explore taxicab numbers
misconceptions: Confuses cubing with multiplying by 3
hooks: Ramanujan’s 1729 taxi story; dice stacked into a big cube

topics.title: Exponential notation and growth
outcomes: Learner can write repeated multiplication in exponential form and compare the growth of powers
misconceptions: Reads 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6
hooks: Folding a paper 10 times; how fast WhatsApp forwards spread

topics.title: Laws of exponents
outcomes: Learner can use laws of exponents to simplify products, quotients and powers of powers
misconceptions: Adds the bases when multiplying powers (2³ × 3² = 5⁵)
Thinks a⁰ = 0
hooks: Simplify 10⁴ × 10³ by counting zeros

topics.title: Negative exponents and scientific notation
outcomes: Learner can interpret negative exponents as reciprocals and write very large and very small numbers in scientific notation
misconceptions: Believes a negative exponent makes the number negative
hooks: Distance to the Sun; size of a bacterium

topics.title: Early number systems
outcomes: Learner can compare tally, Egyptian, Roman and other early number systems and their limitations
misconceptions: Thinks Roman numerals have a zero
hooks: Roman numerals on clock faces and book chapters

topics.title: The idea of a base and place value
outcomes: Learner can explain how a base-10 place-value system with zero works and represent numbers in other bases
misconceptions: Believes base-10 is the only possible way to write numbers
hooks: How computers count in base 2; Brahmi and Hindu numerals

topics.title: Properties of rectangles and squares
outcomes: Learner can state and justify properties of sides, angles and diagonals of rectangles and squares
misconceptions: Thinks a square is not a rectangle
hooks: Why are door frames rectangles? check diagonals with a string

topics.title: Angle sum of a quadrilateral
outcomes: Learner can show that the angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360° by splitting into triangles
misconceptions: Believes bigger quadrilaterals have bigger angle sums
hooks: Tear and arrange the four corners of a paper quadrilateral

topics.title: Parallelogram, rhombus, kite and trapezium
outcomes: Learner can classify quadrilaterals by their properties and show how they are related in a hierarchy
misconceptions: Thinks a rhombus must be "tilted" and a square cannot be a rhombus
Believes a parallelogram must have unequal adjacent sides
hooks: Kites made for Uttarayan; shapes of road signs

topics.title: Checking divisibility quickly
outcomes: Learner can use and justify divisibility rules for 3, 4, 8, 9 and 11 using place value
misconceptions: Applies the divisibility-by-3 test to check divisibility by 6 alone
hooks: Quick check: is a 13-digit Aadhaar-style number divisible by 9?

topics.title: Digits in disguise
outcomes: Learner can solve cryptarithm puzzles using parity, carries and divisibility
misconceptions: Assumes a letter can repeat a digit used by another letter
hooks: Decode a secret message puzzle

topics.title: Distributive property
outcomes: Learner can use the distributive property to multiply expressions and calculate mentally
misconceptions: Writes a(b + c) = ab + c

topics.title: Special products: (a + b)², (a − b)², (a + b)(a − b)
outcomes: Learner can derive and use standard identities with area diagrams
misconceptions: Believes (a + b)² = a² + b²
hooks: Area of a square plot extended on two sides; 99² mentally

topics.title: Mind the mistake
outcomes: Learner can find and fix errors in algebraic manipulations
misconceptions: Thinks −(a − b) = −a − b
hooks: Debug a friend’s homework

topics.title: Ratios and their simplest form
outcomes: Learner can express comparisons as ratios and simplify them
misconceptions: Treats a ratio as a difference (2:3 → 4:5 by adding 2)
hooks: Chai recipe: milk to water ratio

topics.title: Problem solving with proportional reasoning
outcomes: Learner can decide whether two quantities are proportional and solve problems using unit rates
misconceptions: Assumes every relationship is proportional (e.g. age and height)
hooks: Petrol cost for different distances

topics.title: Unit conversions
outcomes: Learner can convert between units using proportional reasoning
misconceptions: Multiplies instead of divides when converting to a larger unit
hooks: Converting km/h to m/s for a train

topics.title: Fractions as percentages
outcomes: Learner can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
misconceptions: Thinks a percentage can never exceed 100
hooks: Exam marks out of 80 shown as a percentage

topics.title: Percentage of a quantity
outcomes: Learner can find a percentage of a quantity and the whole from a part
misconceptions: Believes 20% of 50 and 50% of 20 are different
hooks: GST on a restaurant bill

topics.title: Using percentages: increase, decrease, profit, discount
outcomes: Learner can solve problems on percentage increase and decrease, profit, loss and discount
misconceptions: Thinks a 20% rise followed by a 20% fall returns to the original price
hooks: Festival sale: 30% off then 10% extra

topics.title: Doubling and halving a square
outcomes: Learner can construct a square of double area and relate it to the diagonal
misconceptions: Thinks doubling the side doubles the area
hooks: Baudhayana’s Shulba Sutra fire-altar constructions

topics.title: The theorem for right triangles
outcomes: Learner can state and use the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem to find unknown sides
misconceptions: Applies the theorem to triangles that are not right-angled
Adds the two longest sides’ squares
hooks: Length of a ladder against a wall

topics.title: Integer right triangles (triples)
outcomes: Learner can generate Pythagorean triples and test whether three numbers form one
misconceptions: Believes multiples of a triple are not triples
hooks: 3-4-5 rope trick used by masons to get right angles

topics.title: Ratios in maps and three-term ratios
outcomes: Learner can use map scales and ratios with more than two terms
misconceptions: Scales ratios by adding instead of multiplying
hooks: Cement : sand : gravel = 1 : 2 : 4

topics.title: Dividing a whole in a given ratio
outcomes: Learner can share a quantity in a given ratio
misconceptions: Divides by the larger ratio term instead of the total of parts
hooks: Split a ₹1200 prize in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5

topics.title: Pie charts
outcomes: Learner can read and draw pie charts by converting proportions to angles
misconceptions: Thinks the angles in a pie chart can add up to more than 360°
hooks: How a family spends its monthly budget

topics.title: Inverse proportion
outcomes: Learner can recognise inversely proportional quantities and solve problems
misconceptions: Assumes "more workers, more days" (treats inverse as direct)
hooks: Workers needed to build a wall faster

topics.title: Fractals
outcomes: Learner can describe how simple rules repeated give fractals and count parts at each stage
misconceptions: Thinks fractals are only computer art, not found in nature
hooks: Fern leaves, cauliflower, Sierpinski triangle in rangoli

topics.title: Visualising solids: nets and views
outcomes: Learner can draw nets and views of solids and verify Euler’s formula F + V − E = 2 for polyhedra
misconceptions: Believes any arrangement of six squares folds into a cube
hooks: Open a sweet box to see its net

topics.title: The mean as a balancing act
outcomes: Learner can interpret the mean as a balance point and compute it
misconceptions: Thinks the mean is the middle value in the list
hooks: Average marks of a class; average daily temperature

topics.title: Line graphs
outcomes: Learner can read and draw line graphs for data changing over time and describe trends
misconceptions: Joins points in bar-graph data where the in-between values mean nothing
hooks: Your height over the years; Delhi AQI readings through November

topics.title: Why think-of-a-number tricks work
outcomes: Learner can explain number tricks and puzzles using algebraic expressions
misconceptions: Believes checking a few numbers proves the trick always works
hooks: The "your answer is always 3" trick

topics.title: Number pyramids and grids
outcomes: Learner can use algebra to reason about number pyramids, grids and divisibility tricks
misconceptions: Thinks algebra can only be used with x and y
hooks: Number pyramid puzzle competitions

topics.title: Area of parallelograms and triangles
outcomes: Learner can derive and use area formulas for parallelograms and triangles from rectangles
misconceptions: Uses the slant side instead of the perpendicular height
hooks: Area of a slanted parking slot

topics.title: Area of trapeziums and composite figures
outcomes: Learner can find areas of trapeziums and composite shapes by splitting
misconceptions: Adds all side lengths to find area
hooks: Area of a field shaped like a trapezium
